title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

interactions.name: peer_influence_diffusion
interactions.description: Individuals observe neighbors’ mask-wearing and update their adoption state via a weighted-threshold or logistic decision rule.

interactions.name: social_reinforcement_and_sanctions
interactions.description: Repeated exposures and normative pressure increase adoption likelihood; disapproval or fatigue can lead to dropping.

interactions.name: organizational_broadcast
interactions.description: Organizations disseminate pro- or anti-mask messages that modify perceived risk, norms, and trust-weighted adoption propensity.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations with mask policies enforce compliance, affecting immediate behavior and longer-term perceived norms.

interactions.name: misinformation_propagation
interactions.description: Negative or contradictory information spreads via peers or media, decreasing adoption propensity and trust in authorities.

interactions.name: tie_dynamics
interactions.description: Ties form/dissolve based on homophily and conflict over norms; rewiring changes diffusion pathways.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Proportion of individuals wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Overall mask-wearing rate at the end of the simulation.

metrics.name: time_to_majority
metrics.description: Earliest day when adoption rate first reaches or exceeds 50%.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum adoption rate observed during the simulation.

metrics.name: cascade_size_distribution
metrics.description: Distribution of connected components of adopters formed via diffusion, indicating cascade magnitudes.

metrics.name: adoption_by_subgroup
metrics.description: Adoption rates stratified by demographics, location type, or degree centrality.

metrics.name: drop_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which previously adopting agents stop wearing masks.

metrics.name: diffusion_speed
metrics.description: Average daily change in adoption rate during the growth phase.

metrics.name: behavior_reproduction_number
metrics.description: Average number of new adopters directly attributable to one new adopter in the early phase (R_behavior).

metrics.name: policy_effect_size
metrics.description: Difference-in-differences estimate of policy or campaign impact relative to a control scenario.

validation_criteria.name: convergence_check
validation_criteria.description: Adoption rate change magnitude falls below epsilon (e.g., < 0.001) for K consecutive days (e.g., K=14).

validation_criteria.name: sanity_monotonicity
validation_criteria.description: Increasing influence strength or campaign intensity should not reduce adoption in otherwise identical conditions.

validation_criteria.name: reproducibility
validation_criteria.description: With a fixed random seed, repeated runs yield identical trajectories for key metrics.

validation_criteria.name: baseline_stability
validation_criteria.description: With zero campaign and policy enforcement and moderate thresholds, adoption remains near its seeded rate absent strong network effects.
